#!/bin/bash
# Differential test: Python executable vs Node port.
# Program names legitimately differ (argparse uses basename(argv[0])), so they
# are normalised to PROG before comparison.
PY=/workspace/dataset/test2_executable
JS=/output/test2.mjs

run() {
  local kind="$1"; shift
  if [ "$kind" = py ]; then
    out=$("$PY" "$@" 2>&1); rc=$?
    printf '%s' "${out//test2_executable/PROG}"
  else
    out=$(node "$JS" "$@" 2>&1); rc=$?
    printf '%s' "${out//test2.mjs/PROG}"
  fi
  printf '\n[rc=%d]' "$rc"
}

pass=0; fail=0
check() {
  local desc="$1"; shift
  local a b
  a=$(run py "$@")
  b=$(run js "$@")
  if [ "$a" = "$b" ]; then
    pass=$((pass+1))
    printf 'PASS  %s\n' "$desc"
  else
    fail=$((fail+1))
    printf 'FAIL  %s\n--- python ---\n%s\n--- node ---\n%s\n\n' "$desc" "$a" "$b"
  fi

## Three non-obvious things the black-box probing caught

1. **`format_usage()` collapses its own trailing blank line.** `_format_usage` returns `...\n\n`, but it passes back through `HelpFormatter.format_help()`, which strips it to one `\n`. My first version emitted a blank line before every `error:` message — this alone failed 18 of 37 cases.

2. **argparse re-splits the usage string on a regex before wrapping**, so `--a A` becomes two independently wrappable chunks. At `COLUMNS=34` Python emits `[-h] --a` / `A`, not `[-h]` / `--a A`. Reproduced with `/\(.*?\)+(?=\s|$)|\[.*?\]+(?=\s|$)|\S+/g`.

Two fixes came from the self-tests rather than the diff: whoosh's tokenizers recycle a single `Token` object (harmless in Python list comprehensions, but spreading the generator in JS yielded N references to the same token), so the tokenizers now yield a fresh `Token` per match. And my initial `StopFilter` expectations were wrong, not the code — whoosh renumbers positions from the first *surviving* token's original position, so `'the quick brown fox'` gives `quick@1, brown@2, fox@3`.
